sections.h2: Who bills property tax in the city of Champaign
sections.html:
Champaign does not mail a city tax bill. Each parcel in town is billed by the Champaign County Treasurer (also the Collector), and that single bill covers the schools and every other district that overlaps the property. The Champaign County Supervisor of Assessments handles valuation, and because the city matches Champaign City township, one township assessor covers all of it.

Selling is simpler for it. A single PIN identifies the parcel, and two county offices answer your questions, wherever the house sits.

Champaign is a city of about 23 square miles in central Illinois. Population was estimated at 91,195 in mid-2025, with 43.8% of homes lived in by owners, which leaves renters as the larger group. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $210,900, and median gross rent is $1,123. The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign on the east side and Parkland College on the northwest give the market a large student population during the school year.

A landlord selling a rental near campus will often be dealing with tenants and a lease cycle, and the tax bill follows the parcel no matter who lives in it. Older houses, especially those built in the 1980s or earlier, draw close looks at the roof and heating system, so check both before you list.

Demand shifts from one pocket of the city to the next:

  • Downtown Champaign: the historic core with newer mixed-use buildings and a parking deck.
  • Campustown: the Green Street district beside the university, where high-rise student apartments have opened since 2008.
  • North Prospect: a shopping corridor on the city's northern edge.
  • Northwest and west sides: home to Parkland College and St. Thomas More High School.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
Expect your bill in the mail by early May. Half is normally due in June and half in September, and a postmark on the due date counts. The coupon shows the exact dates.

Interest of 1.5% a month builds on late payments. Personal checks are taken through September 30, and a returned payment is void with a $30 charge plus statutory interest.

  • Online or by phone at 217-834-8713, with a card or eCheck. The processing vendor charges a fee.
  • In person at the Treasurer's counter, 102 E. Main Street in Urbana.

Keep the payment confirmation or canceled check. At closing the title company may ask to see proof that the year's installments are paid.

Complaints go to the Board of Review between July 1 and September 10. The office is open 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., Monday through Thursday, and sees people by appointment too. Township assessors value a house on January 1 at one-third of market value, and owners get a change notice from the Supervisor of Assessments ahead of the window.

Collect proof that fits your property: the price you paid if the purchase was recent, an appraisal, and sales of comparable homes nearby. After September 10 the board reviews the complaints and issues written decisions.

Before you file, look at the change notice you received and compare your value with recent sales on your block. If your value is in line with what similar houses sold for, a complaint is unlikely to change anything. If it is higher, a clean set of comparables and your closing statement are the strongest things you can bring. Call the Board of Review during its Monday to Thursday hours if you want to ask how to submit the paperwork.

Every reduction here is taken from equalized assessed value ahead of the tax rate.

sections.h2: Getting the tax side ready before you list
sections.html:
A little groundwork saves trouble at the closing table. Pull your PIN and write down which installments you have paid this year. Look at your last bill for any exemption that is currently applied, and call the Assessment Office at 217-384-3760 if you are unsure, since the buyer will need to apply for their own. Check the change notice for your assessed value too, because a buyer's agent may ask about it.

If the house is a rental, tell the Treasurer where bills should go after the sale. Tenants who pay a share of the tax through rent should hear about the new mailing arrangement from you rather than from a collection notice.

Tax still open after 4:30 p.m. on October 29 is sold to an investor at the county's October 30 sale. Your house is not what gets sold. Afterward you owe the amount sold plus interest and redeem through the County Clerk.

The Clerk mails a Take Notice inside four months of the sale. Redemption usually runs 3 years from the sale date, with exceptions listed in 35 ILCS 200/21-350. Miss it, and the investor can ask the circuit court for a deed.

sections.h2: Selling a Champaign house when tax is still due
sections.html:
Start with the PIN. The Treasurer can tell you which installments are paid, and your title company or attorney can say whether tax is owed for the year. Depending on the closing and recording dates, a bill may be addressed to the previous owner, who has to forward it to the new owner.

With open installments, ask the title company how they will be settled at closing. An early number lets you pick a closing date with room to spare. For a rental, put the tenants' lease end date on the same checklist.

A rough order of steps: pull the PIN, call the Treasurer for the payment status, confirm what the title company will pay from your proceeds, and make sure the buyer's mailing address goes to the Treasurer so the next bill reaches the right person. A cash buyer can usually close around an open installment, and you do not need to repair the house to the standard a lender's appraiser would expect.

  • Assessment Office, exemptions and forms: 217-384-3760.
  • County Clerk, redemption after a tax sale: 217-384-3722.
  • Treasurer's card and eCheck line: 217-834-8713.

faqs.q: Does the city of Champaign collect its own property tax?
faqs.a: No. Bills come from the Champaign County Treasurer, who collects the money for every parcel in the city and passes it on to the districts.

faqs.q: When is Champaign property tax due?
faqs.a: The bill arrives by early May, and the two installments usually fall in June and September. Your coupon lists the dates.

faqs.q: When can I file an assessment complaint for a Champaign home?
faqs.a: From July 1 to September 10, filed with the Champaign County Board of Review. Its office keeps 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. hours, Monday through Thursday.

faqs.q: What is the senior exemption in Champaign?
faqs.a: It takes $5,000 off equalized assessed value if you turn 65 by the end of the assessment year. A separate assessment freeze exists for household income up to $75,000.
